script.base: BUF is a 5-point favorite at LV in a 54 total (implied BUF 29.5, LV 24.5), so the book expects BUF to lead in a high-scoring game. Base script: BUF leans on James Cook (61 carries, 340 yards, 5.57 YPC over weeks 3-5) against an LV run defense allowing 5.40 YPC and 20 runs of 10+, leads by one to two scores after halftime, and does not abandon the run. LV cannot grind with Ashton Jeanty (44 carries, 141 yards, 3.2 YPC) and stays in the pass game through Brock Bowers (34 targets, 312 yards, 323 air yards) to stay inside the total.
script.flip1: Shootout flip: BUF and LV both throw, BUF carries fall toward the low teens, and Cook rush yards die even at a high YPC (12 carries at 5.5 is about 66). BUF receivers and LV Bowers become the paths to 54. The BUF Cook over fails this flip; the LV Bowers over survives it.
script.flip2: Stall or chase flip: BUF jumps ahead and the LV offense goes three-and-out, so Bowers volume never arrives; or LV hangs around or leads, Jeanty and Mike Washington (15 carries, 77 yards) stay in the run game, and BUF chases through the air and cuts Cook's carries. A late BUF clock-kill can still leave Cook cashed before Ray Davis (3 carries, 5 yards) vultures.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and the BUF-LV slip lost because the 54 came as a pass-first game: LV set extra boxes, BUF Cook got about 14 carries and finished in the 60s, and BUF scored through Allen, Shakir, and Coleman into an LV middle that allows 9.11 YPA. On the other leg BUF bracketed LV Bowers, Cousins' flat 0.13 EPA never produced drives, and targets went to LV Jeanty (already 18 in the L3) and Mayer, leaving Bowers around 55-70. A hidden one-game split could also mean one outing carried the 312-yard total, and unlisted wind would cut his 323 air yards. That counter keeps the LV leg a lean and the slip small, but it is not stronger than an LV 5.40 YPC run leak plus a 34-target LV primary receiver, so both legs stay.
